title: Fibre degree bounds multiply under composition (Stacks 03J6)
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. If the integer $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$ and the integer $m$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $g$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound], then $nm$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $g\circ f:X\to Z$: for every $z\in Z$ the fibre $X_z=X\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ of $g\circ f$ is finite over $\kappa(z)$ with $\dim_{\kappa(z)}\Gamma(X_z,\mathcal O_{X_z})\le nm$. In particular a composition of morphisms with universally bounded fibres has universally bounded fibres.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J6 (lemma-composition-universally-bounded), line 15371, and its proof

proof.text: *The fibre of $g$.* Fix $z\in Z$, put $k=\kappa(z)$ [def-weil-residue-field], $Y_z=Y\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $X_z=X\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}k$ (fibres of $g$ and of $g\circ f$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]). Since $m$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $g$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound], $Y_z$ is finite over $k$ with $\dim_k\Gamma(Y_z,\mathcal O_{Y_z})\le m$; by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim] $Y_z\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $B=\Gamma(Y_z,\mathcal O_{Y_z})$ a $k$-algebra and $\dim_kB\le m$. The field $k$ is a local ring whose only prime is $(0)$ and $B$ is a finite $k$-algebra, so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] $B$ has finitely many prime ideals $\mathfrak n_1,\dots,\mathfrak n_r$, all maximal, whose intersection is the nilradical; thus $|Y_z|=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is a finite discrete set. By [lem-weil-pbc-product-of-localizations-at-maximal] the canonical map $B\to\prod_{i=1}^rB_i$, $B_i=B_{\mathfrak n_i}$, is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras with each $B_i$ local, so $\dim_kB=\sum_i\dim_kB_i$. Each $B_i$ is a quotient of $B$ (a factor of the product), hence finite-dimensional over $k$, hence Artinian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian], so its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_iB_i$ is nilpotent [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent]; and $B_i/\mathfrak n_iB_i=\kappa(\mathfrak n_i)=B/\mathfrak n_i=:K_i$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J6 (lemma-composition-universally-bounded), line 15371, sentences 'By assumption the scheme Y_z is finite over Spec(kappa(z)). In particular, the underlying topological space of Y_z is a finite discrete set' and 'Note that B is the product of its localizations B_m ... by Algebra, Lemmas 00J6 and 00JB'

proof.text: *The fibres of $f_z$.* In the diagram $X_z\to Y_z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ over $X\to Y\to Z$ the lower square ($Y_z$) and the outer rectangle ($X_z$) are cartesian, so by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] $X_z=X\times_YY_z$ with projection $f_z:X_z\to Y_z$, and the structure morphism $X_z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $f_z$ followed by $Y_z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. For a point $\mathfrak n_i$ of $Y_z$ with canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K_i\to Y_z$, pasting again [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] gives $F_i:=X_z\times_{Y_z}\operatorname{Spec}K_i\cong X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K_i$ over $\operatorname{Spec}K_i$, where $\operatorname{Spec}K_i\to Y$ is the composite $\operatorname{Spec}K_i\to Y_z\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound-field-points] shows that $F_i$ is finite over $K_i$ with $\dim_{K_i}\Gamma(F_i,\mathcal O_{F_i})\le n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim] $F_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ with $C_i$ a finite $K_i$-algebra, so $|F_i|$ is a finite discrete set [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum]; $F_i$ is the fibre of $f_z$ at $\mathfrak n_i$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], hence homeomorphic to the subspace $f_z^{-1}(\mathfrak n_i)\subseteq X_z$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J6 (lemma-composition-universally-bounded), line 15371, sentence 'The fibres of the morphism f_z : X_z -> Y_z are the fibres of f at the corresponding points of Y, which are finite discrete sets by the reasoning above', with Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J5 for the degree of these fibres

proof.text: *$X_z$ is affine.* $|X_z|=\bigcup_{i=1}^rf_z^{-1}(\mathfrak n_i)$ is a finite union of finite sets, so finite. Every point $x\in f_z^{-1}(\mathfrak n_i)$ is closed in $X_z$: $\{x\}$ is closed in the discrete subspace $f_z^{-1}(\mathfrak n_i)$ (step 2), which is closed in $X_z$ as the preimage under the continuous map $f_z$ of the closed point $\mathfrak n_i$ of the discrete space $|Y_z|$ (step 1). A finite space whose points are closed is discrete (every subset is a finite union of closed points, hence closed, so every complement is closed). Hence by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-affine] $X_z\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A=\Gamma(X_z,\mathcal O_{X_z})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] $f_z:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the ring map $B\to A$ it induces on global sections, and the structure morphisms give $k\to B\to A$; the $k$-algebra structure of $A$ is the one of the degree in [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound].

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J6 (lemma-composition-universally-bounded), line 15371, sentences 'Hence we conclude that the underlying topological space of X_z is a finite discrete set as well. Thus X_z is an affine scheme (... Properties, Lemma 01ZV ...). Write X_z = Spec(A), Y_z = Spec(B), and k = kappa(z). Then k -> B -> A'

proof.text: *The fibres algebraically.* By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $F_i=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B}\operatorname{Spec}K_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_BK_i)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}K_i$, and $A\otimes_BK_i=A\otimes_BB/\mathfrak n_i=A/\mathfrak n_iA$. Isomorphic schemes over $K_i$ have isomorphic $K_i$-algebras of global sections, so by step 2 $\dim_{K_i}(A/\mathfrak n_iA)=\dim_{K_i}\Gamma(F_i,\mathcal O_{F_i})\le n$ for every $i$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J6 (lemma-composition-universally-bounded), line 15371, '(b) for every maximal ideal m of B we have dim_{kappa(m)}(A/mA) <= n'

proof.text: *Decomposition of $A$.* Tensoring the $k$-algebra isomorphism $B\cong\prod_iB_i$ of step 1 with the $B$-module $A$ (tensor product commutes with finite products) gives $A\cong\prod_iA_i$ with $A_i=A\otimes_BB_i$ (the localization of $A$ at $\mathfrak n_i$ as a $B$-module), an isomorphism of $k$-vector spaces; hence $\dim_kA=\sum_i\dim_kA_i$, where each side may a priori be infinite.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J6 (lemma-composition-universally-bounded), line 15371, 'dim_k(A) = sum_m dim_k(A_m) where ... m runs over the maximal ideals of B (not of A)'

proof.text: *Nakayama.* Fix $i$. As $B_i$-modules, $A_i/\mathfrak n_iA_i=A\otimes_BB_i\otimes_{B_i}B_i/\mathfrak n_iB_i=A\otimes_BK_i=A/\mathfrak n_iA$ (steps 1 and 4), a $K_i$-vector space of dimension $d_i\le n$. Choose $a_1,\dots,a_{d_i}\in A_i$ whose images form a $K_i$-basis of $A_i/\mathfrak n_iA_i$ and let $u:B_i^{\oplus d_i}\to A_i$, $(b_j)\mapsto\sum_jb_ja_j$. The induced map $B_i^{\oplus d_i}/\mathfrak n_iB_i^{\oplus d_i}\to A_i/\mathfrak n_iA_i$ is surjective and $\mathfrak n_iB_i$ is nilpotent (step 1), so $u$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent]. Since $u$ is $k$-linear, $\dim_kA_i\le d_i\dim_kB_i\le n\dim_kB_i$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J6 (lemma-composition-universally-bounded), line 15371, 'By the above, and Nakayama's Lemma (Algebra, Lemma 00DV) we see that each A_m is a quotient of B_m^{oplus n} as a B_m-module. Hence dim_k(A_m) <= n dim_k(B_m)' (00DV part (11): I nilpotent, N/IN -> M/IM surjective implies N -> M surjective)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 5, 6 and 1, $\dim_kA=\sum_i\dim_kA_i\le\sum_in\dim_kB_i=n\dim_kB\le nm$. So $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-module, and the structure morphism $X_z=\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] ((2)$\Rightarrow$(1), with the cover of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ by itself, whose preimage $X_z$ is affine with ring map $k\to A$ finite); its degree is $\dim_k\Gamma(X_z,\mathcal O_{X_z})=\dim_kA\le nm$. As $z$ was arbitrary, $nm$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $g\circ f$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. In particular, if the fibres of $f$ and of $g$ are universally bounded, with bounds $n$ and $m$, then those of $g\circ f$ are universally bounded, with bound $nm$.
